newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DUTCH TOAST AJAX'S "MIRACLE" WIN IN MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUTCH TOAST AJAX'S "MIRACLE" WIN IN MADRID.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam were hailed as heroes on Thursday after their "miraculous" 3-2 victory over Atletico Madrid set up a mouth-watering European Cup semifinal clash with holders Juventus.
Described as the "Miracle in Madrid", Amsterdam newspapers praised their team's character to come back from 1-0 down and eventually win in extra-time. The Dutch side won 4-3 on aggregate.
"What a sensation! What a spectacle! Ajax played what was perhaps the most spell-binding game in their history," said the top-selling Telegraaf newspaper.

Newspapers ignored the error-filled nature of the game, instead dwelling on the two occasions that had tipped the tie in Ajax's favour -- goalkeeper Edwin van der Saar's late penalty save and Dani's spectacular long-range strike in extra-time.
But the victory came at a price. Dani and defender John Veldman went for hospital check-ups after suffering shoulder and ankle injuries.

An average 4.1 million people watched the match on television and even members of parliament followed the game. The Algemeen Dagblad reported that a messenger carried a board with the score through the lower chamber as the match unfolded in Madrid.
The semifinal against Juventus gives Ajax the chance to avenge last year's loss to the Italian club in the final.
For some, it was less important to see Ajax win than to silence Jesus Gil, Atletico's volatile chairman.
Prior to the match in Amsterdam, Gil said Ajax's training session was like a scene from the Congo. His comments led Ajax board members to boycott a lunch with Atletico officials.
